parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a hostile national framework (binary birth-sex passports, X markers stopped, entry refusals and fraud-ineligibility exposure, documented strandings) onto a state that mandates birth-sex facilities in government buildings, schools and prisons with fines, bans marker changes outright, enforces via trooper ID checks at restrooms, and sits in a documented 'Do Not Travel' top tier. Enforcement is active, not latent: capitol ID checks, a trans woman arrested and held 24 hours in a men's ward, a school-district investigation escalated. Remedy is absent or adverse; courts have upheld exclusions and denied custody relief. Minor travel adds state care bans, mandated misgendering in schools and parental investigation posture. No near-certain imprisonment on presentation alone, so not 0.15-tier, but universal, unremedied, state-run exposures across every journey stage place this in high risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports/visas issue only birth-sex markers; X markers stopped; officers refuse cases on 'reasonable doubt' about sex and may pursue lifetime fraud findings; travellers report confiscated passports and strandings; trans-athlete entry ban; foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Ongoing litigation against passport policy; existing X passports valid until expiration; limited fraud waivers exist but are rarely automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: State definition act bans marker changes on state licences/certificates; a mismatched federal-state document stack compounds scrutiny at hotels, restrooms and custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy mandates haircuts, hormone withdrawal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; state prison denial of surgery upheld by courts; arrested trans woman held in men's ward 24 hours.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None operative documented; appeals court affirmed denial of care.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An entry or facility dispute can flow into federal or state custody with birth-sex placement and documented abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Universal state birth-sex restroom/changing rule in schools, universities, prisons and government buildings, backed by $25k/$125k fines; trespass offence in some states; troopers checked IDs at capitol restrooms; unclear guidelines produce uneven, invasive enforcement.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Enforcement episode showed trans women with female ID admitted at capitol restrooms; many other states have no ban, but this state's law is in force.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility exclusion is the operative rule here; the traveller cannot rely on other states' policies while in this state.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care banned since 2023; parents face investigation posture; national hospital record subpoenas and insurance reimbursement proposals; emergency/care access not restricted for adults by ward rule here but custody care denial is documented.
care_services.protection: Earlier injunctions temporarily shielded providers; five DAs refused directives; not shown currently operative.
care_services.interaction: A travelling family could be drawn into child-welfare investigation; minor's medication continuity uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders frame transition as 'mutilation', direct prosecution of teachers facilitating transition; counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state definition act erases recognition; statute-to-statute hostility is current law, not rhetoric alone.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders enjoined; the document states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State enforcement (trooper checks, school-district inquiry) operates under the same threat-framing national backdrop.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans minor care, mandates deadnaming/misgendering in schools, bans LGBT student groups, parental-rights amendment; national order directs criminal investigation of facilitation; a travelling trans minor risks outing at school facilities and possible investigation of the guardian.
minors_guardians.protection: Injunctions previously blocked investigation directives; several cities offer local non-discrimination but cannot reach state school law.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian could face mandatory-reporting exposure if the minor accesses or discusses care or identity.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 44 recorded killings of trans women nationally 2008–2025 (no state-specific figure); state hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and prosecutions are rare; state-level violence record undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity on paper; employment discrimination prohibited nationally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police response uncertain; state hate-crime law offers no gender-identity recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Complaint routes have produced exclusion confirmation, not relief; appeals have upheld exclusion and custody denial; licence-renewal status post-act unknown; state violence rate unknown; school-district inquiry unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suits ongoing; some federal orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation uncertainty means operative rules can shift between booking and travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has one birth-sex facility rule with court-confirmed exclusion. This jurisdiction has that same tier-1 rule at state level plus a national document/entry regime, documented police ID checks, an arrest with men's-ward detention, custody abuse nationally, and a care ban for minors — materially more exposure layers, so lower than 0.35.

0.25-D combines a compulsory facility rule, unremedied ward placement and police stops with extortion threats. This dossier matches the unremedied facility rule and ID checks and adds federal document exposure, but shows no police extortion pattern; slightly above 0.25-D.

0.15-E involves near-automatic arrest on sight, weeks of detention and bribes. Here no offence covers presentation itself; trespass requires refusal to depart; enforcement is episodic, not sweeps. That keeps this jurisdiction well above 0.15 despite comparable hostility in tone.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is a federal–state stack: birth-sex documents and entry screening apply at the border to every trans visitor, and inside this state a universal birth-sex facility rule with active enforcement (trooper ID checks, arrest, school-district investigation) removes the main recourse-free exposures' ambiguity — they are documented, current and unremedied. Severity for an outed adult is major-to-severe (60-day misdemeanour, men's-ward detention, custody abuse, care denial) but not execution-tier; frequency of street violence is not established against background rates. The 'Do Not Travel' tiering, care ban and school investigation posture for minors push the family-travel scenario lower. Net: high risk at the upper end of that band, above 0.35's single-rule anchors in breadth but short of organised near-certain detention.
